catalogue_requests.reason:
No catalogue class writes a PID loop. cap.device.configure.v1 writes one parameter per command, while the upstream sends the three loop-1 PID terms in one command, 'PID 1,

,,' (Lake.py:179); splitting it into three writes would change the wire syntax the instrument receives. The extension takes p, i and d with the bounds the upstream GUI labels (Lake.py:124, 129, 134).

No catalogue stop class binds a thermal.zone heater: cap.motion.stop.v1 binds robot.arm, robot.mobile_base and motion.axis. The upstream's heater range 0 is Off (Lake.py:33) and is written as 'RANGE 0' (Lake.py:180), so this extension is both the SAFE-045 safe-state action and the command the e-stop uses.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend: the gate exited 0 on its third run, G1-G9 all pass with no warnings. The evidence state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. The package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run wC-082) and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached, no hardware backend was run, and no human review or hardware test is claimed.

Recon and scope: the card is a driver-pack of several Tkinter instrument programs. All five card entry symbols were confirmed in the clone: Lake:UpdateValues (Lake.py:40), Lake:UpdatePID (Lake.py:154), SR830:ReadSettings (SR830.py:174), SR830:ReadValues (SR830.py:222) and IPS120:UpdateValues (IPS120.py:126). This package binds the Lake Shore 332 only, the recon's recommended first device; the SR830 lock-in and the Oxford IPS120 and ITC503 controllers are different instruments and are NOT COVERED by this package (one package binds one device).

Shape: no DEVIATION FROM THE CARD. The card's ScpiDriver fits: the Lake Shore traffic is static text commands whose words occur verbatim in Lake.py (KRDG?, CRDG?, RANGE?, HTR?, SETP? 1, PID? 1, MOUT? 1, SETP 1,..., MOUT 1,..., PID 1,..., RANGE ...). The upstream defines no class and builds its Tk window at import (Lake.py:191), so importing it is forbidden and there is no upstream class to name as native; the G7 transport path checks the command tokens against the clone, and the fake answers only those commands. The hardware backend would use the SCPI bridge's visa_resource (the upstream hardcodes GPIB0::12::INSTR, Lake.py:47) or host/port; it is not configured here.

Safety: the declared risk is R2 because the controller drives a heater whose high range is 50 W (Lake.py:33), and heating is at least R2 in the safety spec. The upstream text shows no independent hardware e-stop. The x-cap.daanwielens.heater_off.v1 safe-state action writes RANGE 0 (Off), and safety_bindings.estop writes the same command; that action is the SAFE-045 independent stop path, not a hardware stop. The loader refuses the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written R2 package; no hardware run is claimed.

Limits: every Limit cites an upstream GUI label or dictionary (setpoint 4.5-280 at Lake.py:119, P/I 0.1-1000 at Lake.py:124 and 129, D 0-200 at Lake.py:134, manual output 0.0-100.0 at Lake.py:139, heater range 0-3 at Lake.py:33). No bound is operator_required, and no catalogue class default, constructor default or fake value was used as a bound. site-limits.example.json narrows setpoint to 20-280 K, manual output to at most 50 percent and heater range to 0-1; it is illustrative, not a device fact.

Fake: mock_strategy.preferred is transcript, but the clone has no simulator, mock, upstream test or recorded session; its callbacks open the instrument directly and the scripts build a Tk window at import. The fake is therefore a stateful line transport, not a recording; every canned value and reply format is marked '# placeholder' in fake.py and none is used as a fact, limit or reference. It implements the commands of Lake.py only. The upstream never sends an identity query, so idn=False and the driver does not invent an '*IDN?' exchange.

Coverage: the scalar reads and writes of the Lake Shore program are covered; there is no array to leave out. NOT COVERED: the other devices of the repository (SR830, IPS120, ITC503, DACS, getwaveformTek, importTek) and the upstream Tk GUI. The hardware transport, the VISA address and the real instrument's identity prefix were not tested; the upstream hardcodes GPIB0::12::INSTR.

Provenance: the clone stayed read-only; no upstream code was imported or run; the only writes are under this package directory. G4 has no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings; the one G8.NO_UNIT warning of the first run was cleared by giving the integer heater_range the unit '1'. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; the digest above is the digest the last check printed.

License: the clone has no LICENSE file and the card is NOASSERTION with license_class unknown, so publication needs the owner's decision (publish_review is required); no license is claimed.
